title: Deliberative Alignment Stress-Testing via Adversarial Goal Framing

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Direct chain: adversarial bypass of deliberative alignment informs robustness assessment of a specific training intervention. The Apollo/OpenAI partnership results (13% to 0.4%) provide a concrete baseline to stress-test against.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing adversarial prompt wrappers (fictional contexts, split-turn attacks, role authority) is conceptually accessible but requires creative red-teaming skill. The main barrier is accessing open-source models with deliberative alignment fine-tuning, which are limited. Medium compute helps but setup is non-trivial.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple adversarial wrapper types need to be designed and tested. Requires models with deliberative alignment fine-tuning, which may need to be created or approximated. Achievable in 30 hours if scoped to 3-4 wrapper types on one model, but the fine-tuning prerequisite adds risk.
